answer: A sybil defense can rest on unpredictable live spot-checks: at random times, an agent must prove it is doing the work it claims, by completing a fresh task drawn from its own recent history inside a short window. Its record must be crystal clear, matching observed checkpoints rather than asserting progress. One operator running a shale bed of fakes faces costs that scale with every check: each clone needs its own compute and timely reply, and a missed check freezes its standing. Honest agents pass cheaply, holding the real state, while a vault of dormant clones fails together when checked.
